title: OneDrive Photos on Windows: policies for personal account sign-in and app blocking
summary: The rollout and policy claims agree with Microsoft's notice and the cited references. The admin paths stop short of their settings, and the licensing section should distinguish published OneDrive entitlement from unpublished Photos-specific terms.

claims.claim: The planned controls let organisations manage whether users sign in with personal Microsoft accounts.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Open questions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated the personal-account sign-in default in the updated Photos app on managed devices.
claims.quote: Searched: OneDrive Photos Windows 11 personal Microsoft account sign in default DisablePersonalSync; Photos personal sign in Windows 11. Read MC1518030, Photos release notes and use-group-policy: the last states the sync-app default, not the Photos default.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance controls
claims.claim: Microsoft asks organisations using AppLocker packaged-app rules to keep blocking Photos to include Microsoft.OneDrive.Photos.
claims.quote: If you use AppLocker packaged-app rules to block Microsoft Photos, update those rules to include the package Microsoft.OneDrive.Photos if you intend to keep blocking it.

claims.quote: DisablePersonalSync prevents personal OneDrive account sign-in in Photos.

claims.claim: The notice says DisableNucleusSync prevents use of any OneDrive account in Photos.
claims.quote: DisableNucleusSync prevents the use of any OneDrive account in Photos.

claims.claim: These OneDrive policies restrict OneDrive functionality without preventing use of Photos with local content.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: The notice says the Photos update will not be installed on devices affected by DisableStoreApps.
claims.quote: If your organization disables or removes Store-originated apps using DisableStoreApps, the update will not be installed on affected devices.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft recommends sharing the change with help desk staff who may receive questions about the updated experience.
claims.quote: Share this change with your help desk if users may have questions about the updated experience.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn documents no new Photos-specific setting as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: Photos Windows 11 DisablePersonalSync DisableNucleusSync new administrative policy settings; Photos policy OneDrive Windows 11. Read Photos release notes, OneDrive policies, configure-sync-intune, Lists policies and ApplicationManagement CSP; results describe existing or unrelated controls.

claims.claim: Learn describes no autonomous or agent behaviour for the updated Photos app.
claims.quote: Searched: Windows Photos app autonomous agents administrative Photos specific policy; Photos Windows 11 autonomous agent actions. Read Photos release notes: user-facing search, editing and memories are described, not autonomous agent actions; agent results concern other products.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions
claims.claim: Licensing is unknown because no licence requirement specific to the updated Photos experience is published.
claims.quote: OneDrive for work and school accounts is online storage space in the cloud that's provided for individual licensed users in an organization. OneDrive is included in Microsoft 365 and Office 365 plans, in SharePoint plans, and can also be purchased as a standalone plan.
claims.fix: Set licensing.model to included and replace the notes with: 'For work or school OneDrive access, OneDrive is included in Microsoft 365 and Office 365 plans and SharePoint plans, or purchased as a standalone plan. No licence requirement specific to the updated Photos experience is published as of November 2026.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/office365/servicedescriptions/onedrive-for-business-service-description and use the same distinction in Cost and licensing.

claims.where: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has published no meter specific to the updated Photos experience as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: updated Photos Windows 11 OneDrive Photos licensing license price meter requirement; OneDrive service description licensing OneDrive for Business license users. Read Photos release notes, OneDrive service description, MC1518030 and roadmap; no Photos-specific meter stated.

claims.claim: The roadmap, MC1518030 and Photos release notes themselves name no licence for the updated Photos experience.
claims.quote: Searched: updated Photos Windows 11 OneDrive Photos licensing license price meter requirement. Read the complete roadmap record, MC1518030 and Photos release notes; none states a licence requirement for the updated experience.

claims.claim: Work or school OneDrive photos reside in the user's existing OneDrive storage.
claims.quote: With OneDrive, every person can easily store, access, and share their work files in their personal online storage space in the cloud. OneDrive storage is provisioned on a per user basis
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/office365/servicedescriptions/onedrive-for-business-service-description to sources to support the OneDrive storage statement.

claims.where: front matter: cost; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The known change-related costs are indirect policy-review, AppLocker-maintenance and help desk time, supporting a low cost rating.
claims.quote: Review your existing Windows app-management and OneDrive policies, especially rules that intentionally block or remove Photos. If you use AppLocker to block Photos, account for the updated package name. Share this change with your help desk

claims.claim: The printed Intune settings catalog path reaches the OneDrive settings picker used to configure DisablePersonalSync.
claims.quote: Select Devices > Configuration > Create. Platform: Select Windows 10 and later. Profile type: Select Settings catalog. In Configuration settings, select Add settings. In the settings picker, select OneDrive to see all the available settings.
claims.fix: Append ' > Prevent users from syncing personal OneDrive accounts' to controls[0].ui.path and the rendered path. The current path correctly reaches the picker but stops before the setting named at https://learn.microsoft.com/sharepoint/use-group-policy#prevent-users-from-syncing-personal-onedrive-accounts.

claims.claim: Setting HKCU\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\OneDrive DisablePersonalSync to DWORD 1 enables the personal OneDrive sync restriction.
claims.quote: Enabling this policy sets the following registry key value to 1: [HKCU\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\OneDrive]"DisablePersonalSync"=dword:00000001

claims.claim: DisablePersonalSync is a user-configuration policy stored under HKCU.
claims.quote: User Configuration policies. Prevent users from syncing personal OneDrive accounts. [HKCU\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\OneDrive]"DisablePersonalSync"=dword:00000001

claims.claim: Learn describes DisablePersonalSync for the OneDrive sync app, rather than documenting its Photos-specific effect.
claims.quote: This setting lets you block users from signing in with a Microsoft account to sync their personal OneDrive files.

claims.claim: Windows Components > Store is the Group Policy location for DisableStoreApps.
claims.quote: Name | DisableStoreApps; Friendly Name | Disable all apps from Microsoft Store; Location | Computer Configuration; Path | Windows Components > Store
claims.fix: Replace controls[1].ui.path and the rendered path with 'Computer Configuration > Windows Components > Store > Disable all apps from Microsoft Store', carrying the documented location into the path and ending at the setting rather than its containing Store page.

claims.claim: The Device ApplicationManagement DisableStoreOriginatedApps CSP URI accepts integer 1 to disable Store-app launch.
claims.quote: ./Device/Vendor/MSFT/Policy/Config/ApplicationManagement/DisableStoreOriginatedApps; Format | int; Access Type | Add, Delete, Get, Replace; 1 | Disable launch of apps.

claims.claim: DisableStoreApps turns off launch of all preinstalled or downloaded Microsoft Store apps, not just Photos.
claims.quote: Disable turns off the launch of all apps from the Microsoft Store that came pre-installed or were downloaded.

claims.claim: Apps affected by DisableStoreApps will not be updated.
claims.quote: Apps won't be updated. Your Store will also be disabled.

claims.claim: Learn describes this setting as applying only to Enterprise and Education editions of Windows.
claims.quote: This setting applies only to Enterprise and Education editions of Windows.

claims.claim: DisableStoreApps is a computer-scope policy.
claims.quote: Scope: Device, not User. Group policy mapping: Location | Computer Configuration

claims.claim: Learn documents DisableNucleusSync as the registry value for the Lists policy Prevent Lists sync from running on this device, whose policy name is DisableListSync.
claims.quote: (DisableListSync) Prevent Lists sync from running on this device. This policy's registry value name DisableNucleusSync differs from the policy name DisableListSync. When verifying this policy is applied, look for DisableNucleusSync in the registry.

claims.claim: The notice does not state the roles needed to configure each policy.
claims.quote: Searched: roles and administrator requirements in the supplied MC1518030 notice. Read the complete notice: it names existing management policies but no required administrator role.

claims.claim: The Intune profile requires a Name in Basics before selecting Next.
claims.quote: In Basics, enter the following properties: Name: Enter a descriptive name for the profile. Description: Enter a description for the profile. This setting is optional, but recommended. Select Next.

claims.claim: DisablePersonalSync can be configured through Group Policy or Intune.
claims.quote: Prevent users from syncing personal OneDrive accounts. Applies to: Group Policy, Intune

claims.claim: The Lists sync policy page does not mention Photos.
claims.quote: Searched: Photos Windows 11 DisablePersonalSync DisableNucleusSync new administrative policy settings. Opened and read the complete https://learn.microsoft.com/sharepoint/lists-sync-policies: it documents Lists sync and DisableNucleusSync but does not mention Photos.

claims.claim: Setting DisableNucleusSync affects Lists sync, so its Lists effect needs consideration before configuration for Photos.
claims.quote: If you enable this policy, Lists sync will be blocked from running on the device. Prevent Lists sync from running on the device: [HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\OneDrive] "DisableNucleusSync" = "dword:1"
